trust_decision.summary: pruneBackups decides which directory to delete recursively by trusting the `path` field parsed from each on-disk backup _manifest.json, in EnvironmentManager (lib/env-manager.ts).

landing_point.why: The summary names backup pruning and manifest-driven recursive deletion; pruneBackups' rmSync(entry.path) is the only recursive delete in lib/.

fix_sites.entry_point: EnvironmentManager.pruneBackups() public API; CLI `network-ai env backup prune` (bin/cli.ts:464-473); also reached implicitly from backup() (lib/env-manager.ts:463)
fix_sites.module_kind: core library class (same module as landing point)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published fix for this advisory is one hunk in pruneBackups (fix.diff:345-356); the other hunks in the commit belong to four separate GHSAs (fix.diff:97-101).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: After the fix, the remaining manifest trust (backupId and timestamp choose WHICH backup under .backups/ is deleted) can be argued to be 'only inside the backups dir, so not path traversal'. The restore --latest route can be argued to be the restore advisory's problem, not pruning.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate retention must keep working: backup() auto-prunes to backupRetain and `env backup prune --keep N` must still delete the oldest real backups. The absolute manifest `path` legitimately goes stale if the data dir is moved, so a fix that refuses to prune when entry.path != the computed path (or skips entries it cannot validate) silently stops retention. Deleting the just-created backup would break the promote-then-rollback flow.

O6_input_shapes: manifest `backupId` containing separators or dots (rejected by /^[\w\-]+$/ in fix.diff:353)
backupId resolving outside one level under .backups (dirname check in fix.diff:354-355)

O7_producer.where: lib/env-manager.ts:453-460 (backup() writes BackupEntry with absolute path into _manifest.json); consumed by listBackups lib/env-manager.ts:511-517

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Identity differential: pruneBackups (even after fix) trusts manifest backupId and manifest timestamp instead of the directory name from readdir, so a poisoned manifest can name another real backup (e.g. the newest) for deletion, or sort itself as newest to evict real backups.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The deletion stays inside .backups/ and the advisory talks about arbitrary-path deletion, so 'within the backups dir' looks safe.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same function chain (listBackups -> pruneBackups)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CLI `env backup restore --latest` takes backupId from the newest manifest (manifest-controlled timestamp and backupId) and feeds it to restore(), whose path join has no check at the pinned commit. The sink is a copy, not a deletion, and restore() first calls backup(), which prunes.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The sink is a copy, not rmSync, and restore traversal is a separate advisory (GHSA-48x2) fixed in the same commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a public deleteBackup(env, backupId) / CLI `env backup delete` that removes listBackups()[i].path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Natural companion to prune; a maintainer would reuse BackupEntry.path from listBackups exactly as prune did.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: rollback cleanup that removes the restored backup by the manifest path after a successful rollback
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Transport already holds backup ids and manages the rollback lifecycle; this would sit in another file and add distance from the landing point.

O9_family: CWE-22/CWE-73 path traversal via externally controlled persisted file path (trusted manifest field drives recursive delete)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm, tsc, ts-node (package.json:33-64); runtime dependency commander
O10_build.project_tests: test-env-manager.ts section 11 backup/restore/prune (test-env-manager.ts:445-501); run via npx ts-node test-env-manager.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate entry.path with a startsWith(backupsDir) check, or recompute the path from manifest backupId (the published fix), while still trusting manifest backupId/timestamp for identity and order.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit bundles 5 GHSAs (symlink backup, restore traversal, sandbox prefix, ApprovalInbox auth) in lib/env-manager.ts, lib/agent-runtime.ts and lib/approval-inbox.ts; only the pruneBackups hunk is this advisory.
lib/locked-blackboard.ts:557-574,661-667: change_id read from on-disk pending_changes JSON builds an unlink path; same persisted-metadata-to-path idea, but a different module and sink.
bin/cli.ts:466 parseInt --keep can yield NaN, so all.slice(NaN) would prune every backup (lib/env-manager.ts:531-533); this is a retention logic issue, not this protection.
